record.question: A mother who is a carrier for hemophilia asks about risk. Which child is MOST likely to have the disease?
record.explanation: Answer B: Son. Hemophilia A/B are X-linked recessive; a carrier mother can pass the affected X chromosome to a son, who is more likely to express the disorder than a daughter in the usual scenario. Source/context note: Each pregnancy is independent; daughters can be affected in uncommon inheritance combinations. Reference: https://www.cdc.gov/hemophilia/about/index.html. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
